newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool indicator falls 2 cents to 753c/kg.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool indicator falls 2 cents to 753c/kg.

text.p: The eastern market indicator eased back two cents to 753 cents a kg clean on Thursday at wool sales in Sydney and Adelaide, Wool International said.
Merino fleece was mixed, with 19 micron slightly dearer, 20m one percent dearer, 21m 0.5 percent dearer, 22/23 one percent cheaper, 24m two percent cheaper and 25/26m 1.5 percent cheaper.
In merino skirtings, 19/20/21m were generally unchanged while 22/23m were one percent cheaper.
In crossbreds, 27/28/29m were 0.5 percent cheaper, 30m unchanged and 31m 0.5 percent dearer, while cardings were generally unchanged.
WI said trading saw good general competition from most sectors.
Of the 21,395 bales offered, 2.8 percent were passed in.

In early Fremantle trading, merino fleece was mostly cheaper, with 20/21m one percent cheaper, 22m 1.5 percent cheaper, 23m generally unchanged, 24m two percent cheaper and 25m one percent cheaper. Locks were generally unchanged.
The offering was 9,681 bales and the early pass-in rate 15.5 percent.
Sales continue next week in Sydney and Melbourne with about 72,600 bales to be offered.
